task.description: WF-03 Step 3d REVIEWER gate (idiom / supervision integrity / scope creep / decision-record consistency) on ISS-0227 (GH#465, queue task 227), branch fix/WF03-ISS0227-20260822 at HEAD 7b880a1. REVIEWER filed this issue during WF03-ISS0224-20260822, so this gate additionally judges whether what shipped addresses what was filed. Sole code change: cbdda6f -- lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex, 5 hunks. Everything else on the branch is design docs and handoffs. test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs is TEST-DESIGNER's concurrent work in the same checkout and was read informationally only; it is gated by TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, not here.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The shipped change actually removes the two filed write-only derivable fields, introduces no third copy of either fact, and the promised derivations (elem(p.from, 0); the schema name off in_flight.op) are available at every point a future reader would need them.

2. Invariant integrity verified by reading, not by trusting the diff's size: owner_ref intact everywhere; the monitor still established at reservation from the local in reserve_slot/2; clause B's ordered classification (1, 2, 3, 4, 4b, 5, no-op) untouched; the serialized-DB-worker property (in_flight nil-or-one) untouched; db_queue's 2 x max_concurrent bound argument still sound with the smaller record.
3. OTP idiom: derive-at-point-of-use vs. a memoized copy, given pump/1 runs inside a callback; whether the removed memoization was load-bearing for latency on any hot path.

4. The supersede treatment of iss0224-sandbox-pool-async-provisioning.md (C1-C5) follows the in-place-marker convention the design's 5.1 derived from three in-repo precedents; the new section 17 is accurate; the record now agrees with the code.
5. Decision-record consistency and scope creep: nothing in docs/migration/decisions/ silently re-decided; no renames, no reordering, no added accessor helper, no 'while I'm here' improvements.

6. Rule on CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR round 2's non-blocking MINOR: R1 and R3 are the two removals no runtime test can observe -- are both adequately discharged, and is R3's omission from the design's coverage map worth a follow-up?

7. Rule on two candidate docs/anti-patterns.md entries surfaced by this run: (a) the grep-shaped-criterion recurrence in a new medium; (b) verifying a mix-gate property with a non-mix probe. If either should be written now, give the exact text and its location.

result.summary:
PASS. Reviewed at branch HEAD 7b880a1. `git diff --stat 233af04..7b880a1` is five files: four handoff/design documents plus lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex. The only code change is cbdda6f's five hunks in sandbox_pool.ex. I read the module in full post-change (901 lines), the ISS-0227 design in full, the ISS-0224 design's sections 5, 7 step 2, 8.4 and the new 17, and all four handoffs. Every line number below is from my own read of the post-change file at 7b880a1; pre-change line numbers are from `git show 233af04:lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex`.

=== 1. AS THE FILER: does this fix what I filed? YES, exactly and only that. ===

I filed two write-only derivable fields during WF03-ISS0224-20260822 (merge b8ebfb0), declining to mint an id per ISSUE_QUEUE.md. Both are gone, and the removal set is exactly the design's R1-R5 with nothing added.

Pre-change positions, confirmed against 233af04: owner_pid at :160 (the @typep line), :527 (the local), :528 (the monitor), :535 (the op literal); schema_name at :316 (the state-shape comment) and :572 (pump/1's in_flight literal); op_schema_name/1 at :592-593. These are the design's cited line numbers verbatim -- I re-derived them rather than inheriting them, and all five landed.

  (a) FIELD 1 GONE. `@typep provision_op` now runs :158-164 with five fields -- from, owner_ref, sandbox_id, schema_name, owner_down? -- in their original order, no owner_pid. reserve_slot/2's op literal at :529-537 carries the same five, same order. The ONLY surviving `owner_pid` token in the entire module is the local at :525, read one line later at :526 by `Process.monitor/1`. That is the design's 2.1 carve-out and W10, and it is correct: deleting it would be an undefined-variable compile error at :526.

  (b) FIELD 2 GONE. pump/1's in_flight literal at :565-569 is exactly `%{op: op, task_ref: task.ref, task_pid: task.pid}` -- three keys. The state-shape comment's in_flight block at :311-315 declares the same three and is still well-formed pseudo-map syntax (the trailing comma was correctly dropped from `task_pid: pid()`).

  (c) NO THIRD COPY OF EITHER FACT. `grep -rn "owner_pid" --include=*.ex --include=*.exs .` over the repo returns, outside deps/ and scratch/ (both gitignored): sandbox_pool.ex:525 and :526 (the local and its monitor) and test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:420/443/444/445 (an unrelated local for a spawned test process -- W3, verified by read). `git grep -lF "in_flight.schema_name"` returns no code file at all. There is no accessor helper: no `defp owner_pid(`, no `defp op_schema_name`, nothing reintroducing a second source of truth -- design section 8 item 4 honoured.

  (d) THE PROMISED DERIVATIONS ARE GENUINELY AVAILABLE, at every point a future reader would need them.
      owner_pid -> `elem(p.from, 0)`: `from` survives on provision_op (:159) and is populated at :532 from reserve_slot/2's own argument. It is read on both live provision-completion paths (:614 `GenServer.reply(p.from, ...)`, :625, :677), so it is not itself at risk of becoming dead. Crucially it is NEVER REWRITTEN on a provision op: the single in-place rewrite this module performs on one is `owner_down?: true` at :446 (`%{p | owner_down?: true}`), which touches no other key. So the derivation cannot drift from what the removed field held.
      in_flight.schema_name -> the schema name off `in_flight.op`: both op kinds retain `schema_name` in their typespecs (:162 for provision_op, :174 for drop_op), and every existing consumer already reaches it that way -- run_op/1 at :582 and :586 destructure the op tuple, handle_worker_death/1 reads `p.schema_name` at :668 off in_flight.op. The two in_flight map-update sites (:446, :720) both update the `op` key only, so the op-and-therefore-the-name is always present on the record. TEST-DESIGNER's own pre-existing sites at test:920 and :1007 already read `{:provision, %{schema_name: o_schema}} = state.in_flight.op`, which is direct evidence the derived form was the natural one all along.

  VERDICT ON ITEM 1: the fix is exactly what I filed, no more and no less. It also does not overreach: design OQ-2 explicitly records that no module-wide dead-field audit was performed and that section 2's removal set must not be read as 'the complete set of dead fields'. That is the right scope discipline for a MINOR issue and I endorse it.

=== 2. INVARIANT INTEGRITY -- verified by reading, with line numbers ===

The load-bearing question is not 'is the diff small' but 'does any invariant of ISS-0224 read a key that no longer exists, or depend on a count the removal changes'. Answer: no, on five independent checks.

  (i) owner_ref INTACT EVERYWHERE. I enumerated every occurrence in the post-change file: typespec :160 (provision_op) and :177 (drop_op); reserve_slot/2 :526 (established) and :533 (stored); handle_call({:release,_}) :346 (read out of the active entry) and :362 (copied into the drop op); complete_op/3 :611 (into the active entry), :624 (demonitor on provision failure), :634 (demonitor on successful release); handle_worker_death/1 :676; orphan_release_drop/3 :712 (cleared to nil on the retarget); the reclaim/orphan literals :487, :603, :671 (nil by design); and the five lookup helpers at :773, :778, :790, :802, :814/:820. NOT ONE of those lines appears in `git show cbdda6f`. The diff's five hunks touch :160, :315-316, :535, :571-572 and :591-593 of the pre-change file and nothing else.

  (ii) THE MONITOR IS STILL ESTABLISHED AT RESERVATION, FROM THE LOCAL. reserve_slot/2 (:524-540) is byte-identical apart from the single deleted `owner_pid: owner_pid,` line. Order is unchanged: :525 binds the local from `elem(from, 0)`, :526 monitors it, :527 mints the identity, :539 enqueues. So the monitor is still taken on the CALLING process, strictly before mint_sandbox_identity/0 and therefore strictly before any schema can exist -- the no-monitor-gap property INV-SP-A4 rests on. The moduledoc's 'A slot is reserved -- and its owner monitored -- before any DB work starts' (:74-76) and the same-process claim/release contract section (:33-46) both remain true verbatim. The header comment at :518-522, which explains why the monitored ref is the caller's and never the worker's, is untouched and still accurate.

  (iii) CLAUSE B'S ORDERED CLASSIFICATION IS UNTOUCHED. handle_info({:DOWN, ...}) runs :418-503. The cond arms are, in order: case 1 worker death :425; case 2 owner-down-mid-provision :436; case 3 parked waiter :449; case 4 queued provision :455; case 4b queued-or-in-flight release drop :465; case 5 ISS-0048 reclaim :474; case 6 no-op :499. 4b STILL PRECEDES 5 -- the R2-F1 ordering fix. The explanatory comment at :407-417 that says why ('letting case 5 win instead would delete the active entry AND enqueue a SECOND drop for the same schema, breaking the db_queue bound') is intact. None of these lines is in the diff. The discriminators are `state.in_flight.task_ref` (:425), `in_flight_provision_owner_ref(state)` (:436, defined :778-779 matching `%{in_flight: %{op: {:provision, p}}}`), and three owner_ref lookups -- every one of them reads `.task_ref` or `.op`, never a removed key.

  (iv) THE SERIALIZED-DB-WORKER PROPERTY IS STRUCTURAL AND UNTOUCHED. It is enforced by pump/1's clause head `defp pump(%{in_flight: nil} = state)` at :560 plus the catch-all `defp pump(state), do: state` at :578 -- a match on nil-ness of the whole field, not on any field inside the record. Making the record smaller cannot affect a nil test. Every site that clears it writes `in_flight: nil` (:606, :616, :628, :640, :657, :680, :692) and the single site that sets it is pump/1 :565-571. So 'nil or exactly one record' still holds by construction, and the moduledoc's :60-62 claim ('there is nowhere to put a second, and the serialization is structural rather than an invariant to maintain') stands.

  (v) THE db_queue 2 x max_concurrent BOUND ARGUMENT IS STILL SOUND, and the reason is worth stating rather than assuming: THE BOUND COUNTS OPS, NOT FIELDS. It is an in-contract bound on how many op TUPLES can coexist in db_queue -- at most one {:provision,_} and at most one {:drop,_} per slot -- and it is computed, where the code computes it at all, by provision_ops_pending/1 (:734-738), which matches `{:provision, _}` on the op tuple and `match?(%{op: {:provision, _}}, state.in_flight)` on the in_flight record. That last match names the `op` key ONLY, which is precisely why deleting a sibling key of `op` cannot perturb it. A record with three keys carries exactly the same one op a record with four did. Case 4b's no-second-drop retarget (orphan_release_drop/3 :707-725) is likewise a map-update on `d` preserving schema_name, plus `%{new_state.in_flight | op: orphaned}` at :720 -- again the `op` key only. Bound unaffected.

  (vi) ONE EXPLICIT CRASH CHECK, because a missing map key is a crash in a supervised GenServer, not a warning. Elixir's `%{m | k: v}` update syntax raises KeyError on a MISSING key. The only two in_flight updates are :446 and :720; both update `op`, which exists on every in_flight record pump/1 builds. There is no `Map.get/fetch/take/has_key?/pop` anywhere on in_flight or on an op (the module's only Map.* lookup is `Map.fetch(state.active, sandbox_id)` at :342, on `active`), and no `in_flight[:schema_name]` access. So no reader, static or dynamic, can miss the removed key.

  MY OWN MEASUREMENTS, run in this worktree rather than quoted from ELIXIR-DEV's report: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> exit 0, no output, no unused-function warning (this is the positive evidence that R5 landed -- had op_schema_name/1 been retained, this is the command that goes red). `mix format --check-formatted` -> exit 0 (R3/R4's comma removals are exactly the edit that drifts formatting). GH #465 AC4 in its code-restricted form, `git grep -nE "owner_pid:|schema_name: op_schema_name|op_schema_name" -- 'lib/**/*.ex' 'test/**/*.exs'` -> no output, exit 1. I did not run mix test: TEST-DESIGNER is writing in this checkout and a concurrent suite run is its call to make, not mine.

=== 3. OTP IDIOM: derive at the point of use is right, and the memoization was not load-bearing ===

PASS, and stronger than 'harmless'. Three grounds, all from the code.

  (a) THERE WERE ZERO READERS, so there was no latency to preserve -- confirmed independently of the design by my own greps in item 1(c). A memoized value nobody reads costs one extra map key per op dispatched and buys nothing measurable, because nothing measures it.

  (b) NO HOT PATH EXISTS HERE, by two orders of argument. pump/1 runs once per DB op, and the moduledoc's own measurement (:52-56) puts one provisioning at 411 ms at its very fastest -- a CREATE SCHEMA plus 31 migrations. Both derivations are O(1) and allocation-free: `elem(p.from, 0)` is a tuple-element read on a 2-tuple, and the schema name off in_flight.op is a single pattern match on a 2-tuple. Deriving at the point of use is invisible against the DB work it accompanies by roughly nine orders of magnitude. And the change strictly REDUCES callback work: pump/1 now does one fewer function call and one fewer map insertion per dispatch, inside the callback that the whole ISS-0224 design exists to keep short.

  (c) IT MAKES THE MODULE MORE CONSISTENT WITH ITS OWN STATED IDIOM, which is the point that decides it for me. The comment at :781-783, written by ISS-0224 itself, justifies linear-scanning a small bounded collection as 'preferred over a separately-maintained counter or index, which would be a second source of truth for the same fact.' The two removed fields were exactly that -- a second source of truth for a fact the record already carried. Keeping them would have left the module arguing against itself in two comments twelve hundred lines apart. Removing them is the idiomatic call, not merely the tidy one.

  On the specific 'pump/1 runs inside a callback' concern: that cuts the same way. Work done inside a GenServer callback is work during which the mailbox is frozen, which is the exact pathology ISS-0224 was filed to fix. Memoizing inside a callback to save work on a read that happens outside the callback would be a defensible trade; memoizing inside a callback to save work on a read that never happens is pure cost. Correct call.

=== 4. THE SUPERSEDE TREATMENT OF iss0224-...md (C1-C5) ===

PASS on all three sub-questions: it follows the convention, section 17 is accurate, and the record now agrees with the code.

  FOLLOWS THE CONVENTION. I checked the landed text against the design's 5.2-5.6 instructions character by character. C1 (:507): the removed `owner_pid:   pid(),` line is replaced IN PLACE by `# owner_pid REMOVED by ISS-0227 (2026-08-22) -- write-only; derive as elem(p.from, 0). See section 17.`, inside the fence, at the removed field's own position, with the surviving five fields neither reordered nor renumbered (:506, :508-511 read from / owner_ref / sandbox_id / schema_name / owner_down? -- original order). C2 (:522-527): same treatment for in_flight's schema_name, plus the trailing comma correctly dropped from `task_pid:    pid()` so the pseudo-map stays well-formed. C3 (:808-811): :808's prose describing the two surviving LOCAL bindings is correctly left alone (it still describes what reserve_slot/2 does), :810's enumerated literal drops `owner_pid:,`, and the one-line removal note is appended after it. C4: section 17 appended after section 16 in precedent 2's heading shape. C5 (:6-10): the dated top-of-file pointer sits immediately after the Status line and before the round-1 REWORK NOTICE, in precedent 1's shape. The design's own justification for using a comment line rather than strikethrough -- strikethrough does not render inside a fenced block -- is correct and is the right adaptation of precedent 3 to this medium.

  SECTION 17 IS ACCURATE. I checked its four checkable claims against the code. 'Both are gone from lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex' -- true (item 1). '`from` ... is never rewritten on a provision op -- the only in-place rewrite this module performs on one is owner_down?: true' -- true, that is :446 and it is the only one. 'case 4b's rewrite changes only from/owner_ref/purpose' -- true, :712. 'op_schema_name/1 ... had no call site left, and an unused defp fails mix compile --warnings-as-errors' -- true and I measured the consequent myself (exit 0 post-removal). Its no-invariant-change paragraph correctly types both removed values out of INV-SP-A3's scope (a pid() and a String.t(), where A3 classifies reference() values) and correctly grounds INV-SP-A4's five death paths on owner_ref plus the PRE-MINTED schema_name of provision_op/drop_op, both retained.

  THE RECORD NOW AGREES WITH THE CODE. I grepped every remaining owner_pid and schema_name mention in the 1953-line iss0224 document and accounted for all of them: :6 (the C5 pointer), :507 (the C1 marker), :565 (the owner_ref bullet's reference to `Process.monitor(owner_pid)` -- the surviving LOCAL, correctly left verbatim per 5.3), :808/:811 (C3), and :1917-1949 (section 17 itself). Every one either announces the removal or refers to the surviving local. There is NO surviving assertion anywhere in the document that either field exists. I specifically checked the two places most likely to have been missed and neither needed an edit: section 7 step 2's pump/1 prose at :813-816 ends 'and set in_flight' without enumerating its fields, and section 7 step 3's handle_worker_death pseudocode at :940 builds its drop from `p.schema_name` -- off the op, matching the code at :668.

  SMALL CROSS-CHECK OF THE DESIGN'S OWN PREMISE, since I am gating it: W11 claims section 5's field-by-field rationale list has no bullet for in_flight's schema_name and none for owner_pid, so there is no prose rationale to retract. I re-read :555-585 and confirm it. That is why C1/C2 are the complete set of section 5 edits.

=== 5. DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY AND SCOPE CREEP: clean ===

No decision record is touched or re-decided: `git diff --stat 233af04..7b880a1` names five files and none is under docs/migration/decisions/. Nothing in the change bears on 0001-web-framework, 0003 or 0004; this is an internal GenServer state shape with no framework, library, persistence or process-architecture choice in it.

No scope creep, checked item by item against the design's section 8 prohibitions rather than by impression. No rename (every surviving identifier keeps its name). No reordering (the five surviving provision_op fields and the three surviving in_flight keys are in their original relative order in both the typespec and both literals). NO ACCESSOR HELPER -- there is no `defp owner_pid(op)`, no replacement for op_schema_name/1, nothing 'preserving the interface' for a thing nothing called; section 8 item 4 anticipated exactly this temptation and it was resisted. No 'while I'm here' improvement: the five hunks are R1-R5 and the two consequent trailing commas, and nothing else in a 901-line file moved. No new abstraction, no behaviour, no macro, no generic plumbing -- the change is strictly subtractive, which is the opposite of the failure mode this gate watches for.

One scope point worth crediting rather than flagging: the design REFUSED to expand. OQ-1 declines to name `elem(p.from, 0)` until something needs it in more than one place; OQ-2 declines to audit the rest of the state shape for further dead fields and says so explicitly rather than letting silence imply completeness; section 13 reports both as candidate successor issues to ORCH instead of absorbing them. That is the correct discipline and I want it on the record as such.

=== 6. RULING ON R1 AND R3 (the two removals no runtime test can observe) ===

BOTH ADEQUATELY DISCHARGED. R3's omission from the coverage map is genuinely immaterial and warrants NO follow-up. This is my gate to make and I am making it, not deferring it.

  R1 (the `owner_pid: pid(),` @typep line). Discharged by direct read: `@typep provision_op` at :158-164 carries five fields and owner_pid is not among them. I note precisely what my compile run does and does not prove here, because the distinction matters: a @typep is not enforced at runtime and Elixir's compiler does not check map literals against it, so `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` exiting 0 does NOT prove R1 landed -- it would exit 0 with R1 skipped too (only Dialyzer, not run here, would notice). R1 therefore rests on the read, which is exactly what the design says ('compile-time-only, discharged by diff review plus REVIEWER') and exactly what a human-free pipeline needs an independent reader for. I have read it. It landed.

  R3 (the `schema_name: String.t()` line in the state-shape comment). Discharged on two grounds. First, direct read: the in_flight block at :311-315 declares op / task_ref / task_pid and the comment is still well-formed -- the trailing comma was dropped from :314 as specified, so the pseudo-map does not read as truncated. Second, and this is why the omission is immaterial rather than merely minor, R3 IS NOT ACTUALLY UNOBSERVABLE IN THE LONG RUN, it is only unobservable by a test. RT-9's key-set assertion at test:1220 pins the runtime record to exactly [:op, :task_pid, :task_ref]. Had R3 been skipped, the comment at :311-315 and the assertion at test:1220 would visibly contradict each other in a file any future reader of this module opens. So the comment is cross-checked by the suite indirectly, in the only sense a comment can be.

  ON THE COVERAGE MAP'S MISSING R3 ROW: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's MINOR, non-blocking call was right, and I additionally rule it needs no follow-up issue. The map's R1 row already states the discharge mechanism for this entire class -- compile-time-only, diff review plus REVIEWER -- and R3 is the same class with the same mechanism. What is missing is a row in a table, not a discharge. The only work a follow-up could produce is adding a line to a design document's table recording that REVIEWER read a comment, which this handoff already records with more evidence than the row would carry. Filing it would add queue traffic and no verification. Closed here.

=== 7. RULINGS ON THE TWO ANTI-PATTERN CANDIDATES: WRITE BOTH NOW ===

  (a) THE GREP-SHAPED-CRITERION RECURRENCE -- WRITE NOW, but as an AMENDMENT to the existing entry at docs/anti-patterns.md:1195, not a new entry. It is the same failure mode, so a second top-level entry would fragment it; but the amendment is not a cross-reference, because THE CORRECT RESPONSE INVERTS and the existing entry's stated remedy is actively wrong for this medium. The existing entry says reword the prose so it does not contain the flagged substring. That works for a moduledoc, whose subject is the module and which merely mentions what it does not do. It does NOT work for a design document or a handoff whose entire subject IS the removed field -- the design's own 4.1 puts it exactly right: 'A design that cannot name the field it removes is not a design.' For those the remedy is to restrict the criterion by path, which is a different action, and an entry that records the recurrence without recording the inverted remedy would send the next agent to garble a design doc.

  I also correct one figure in the dispatch while endorsing its conclusion, since a gate that passes a false number on is not a gate. The brief said the one file still containing the literal `in_flight.schema_name` is this run's own design doc. At 7b880a1 that is no longer true: `git grep -lF "in_flight.schema_name"` returns FOUR tracked files -- lib/letflow/design/iss0227-sandbox-pool-dead-field-removal.md, lib/letflow/design/iss0224-sandbox-pool-async-provisioning.md (whose new section 17, added by this very run, names the field to record its removal), handoffs/.../step-01-issue-fixer-diagnosis.json and handoffs/.../step-03c-security-reviewer.json. On the ACTUAL AC4 pattern the unrestricted spread is six files. That strengthens the case rather than weakening it: the recurrence is in three media (a live design doc, a superseded design doc, and handoff JSON), not one, and two of them -- the superseded record and the handoffs -- are media the existing entry does not contemplate at all and cannot be reworded even in principle, because a handoff is a frozen audit record. Exact text and location are in issues[0] below, tagged doc-updater-input rather than as a defect.

  (b) VERIFYING A MIX-GATE PROPERTY WITH A NON-MIX PROBE -- WRITE NOW, as a new entry appended at the end of docs/anti-patterns.md (currently 1268 lines; the file's convention is chronological append and the last entry is dated 2026-08-22). Three reasons it should not be deferred. First, there is no existing entry and the two commands share a flag name, share their warning text, and differ only in exit code -- the one thing scrolled output does not show -- so it is a trap that survives careful reading. Second, this project's merge gate IS `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (GIT_MERGE.md:166 and step 3 of mix.exs's letflow.check alias), so a wrong answer here is a wrong answer about whether a merge goes red -- and in THIS run the answer decided R5, whether a private function had to be deleted. Third, deferring loses the measurement: W7/W8 in design section 3.3 are a matched pair run on the same shape, and that provenance is cheap to record now and expensive to reconstruct later. That it was caught rather than suffered is not a reason to defer -- the existing entry at :1195 was also caught before harm (ELIXIR-DEV reworded the moduledoc before the AC ever failed) and was written anyway; CLAUDE.md's rule is to add when you find a mistake worth not repeating, and 'found by the agent who nearly made it' is the normal case. Exact text and location are in issues[1] below.

=== ONE NON-BLOCKING TYPE-SAFETY OBSERVATION (does not affect this PASS) ===

Per my role's item 3 I record it here and route it rather than leaving it in prose only, and -- as when I filed ISS-0227 itself -- I decline to mint an id: ISSUE_QUEUE.md reserves that, and ORCH should decide whether it joins design section 13's two existing candidates. The in_flight record and both op maps are BARE MAPS with @typep map shapes (:158-181, :311-315), not structs. That is ISS-0224's deliberate choice and I am not second-guessing it inside this run. But note what it costs precisely here: because in_flight is a bare map, a future change that re-adds a redundant `schema_name:` key to pump/1's literal is a legal, warning-free, compiling edit, and the ONLY thing standing between it and main is RT-9's key-set assertion -- a runtime test. Had in_flight been a struct with @enforce_keys, the same edit would be a compile-time KeyError and the class of defect I filed as ISS-0227 would be unrepresentable rather than merely detectable. That is the textbook shape of 'an invalid state only a test catches'. Second occurrence of the pattern in this module (the `active` value map at :306-307 is the first), so it is worth watching as the state shape grows rather than acting on now. MINOR, lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex, tag type-safety.

=== VERDICT ===

PASS. The change fixes exactly what I filed, introduces no third copy of either fact, moves no invariant, adds no abstraction, re-decides no decision record, and leaves the ISS-0224 record in agreement with the code. TEST-DESIGNER is unblocked. RT-9 is TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's gate, not mine, and I formed no view on it beyond noting that its :1220 key-set assertion is the mechanism that will keep item 6's R3 honest.

**Recurrence: 2026-08-22, ISS-0227 (`WF03-ISS0227-20260822`) -- same failure, different medium, and the correct response inverts.** GH #465's acceptance criterion 4 was a `git grep` for any remaining writer of two removed `Letflow.SandboxPool` fields (`owner_pid:`, `op_schema_name`). Run unrestricted at branch HEAD it matches **six tracked files and zero lines of code**: both design documents (`lib/letflow/design/iss0227-sandbox-pool-dead-field-removal.md`, and `lib/letflow/design/iss0224-sandbox-pool-async-provisioning.md`, whose new section 17 names the fields in order to record their removal) plus four run handoff JSONs. Two of those media are ones the entry above does not contemplate: `lib/` also contains `lib/letflow/design/*.md`, so a `lib/`-scoped grep does not exclude prose, and `handoffs/**.json` quotes the removed identifiers verbatim by necessity.

**The remedy above does not apply to them.** Rewording works for a moduledoc, whose subject is the module and which merely *mentions* what it does not do. It does not work when the matching text is the file's *subject*: a design document that cannot name the field it removes is not a design, and a handoff is a frozen audit record that must not be reworded at all. For those, **restrict the criterion by path or extension** instead:

```
git grep -nE "<pattern>" -- 'lib/**/*.ex' 'test/**/*.exs'
```

**Correct alternative (generalised).** When writing a grep-shaped acceptance criterion, decide up front which of the two remedies applies: **reword** when the matching text is *incidental* to the file's purpose; **restrict the path** when the matching text is *the file's subject*. Then write the restriction into the criterion itself, so it is runnable exactly as stated. A criterion that only passes once the verifier silently narrows it is not a criterion -- and the narrowing is the step that gets skipped, or done differently, by the next agent.

## `elixirc --warnings-as-errors` is not a proxy for `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -- it gives the opposite answer

**Found:** 2026-08-22, CODE-DESIGNER, ISS-0227 (`WF03-ISS0227-20260822`), recorded as W7/W8 and section 3.3 of `lib/letflow/design/iss0227-sandbox-pool-dead-field-removal.md`. The design had to decide whether deleting a private function's last call site would turn `op_schema_name/1` into a red build, since this project's merge gate is `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (`docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md:166`, and step 3 of `mix.exs`'s `letflow.check` alias). The cheap way to check looks like running `elixirc --warnings-as-errors` on a throwaway `.ex` file -- no project, no deps, one second. **Measured both ways on the same two-clause unused-`defp` shape: `elixirc --warnings-as-errors` prints the "is unused" warning and exits 0; `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` prints the same warning and exits 1** ("Compilation failed due to warnings while using the --warnings-as-errors option"). The cheap probe answers the opposite of the gate that actually runs.

**Why this is easy to miss:** the two commands take the same flag name, emit the same warning text, and differ only in the exit code -- the one thing scrolled terminal output does not show. An agent that eyeballs the warning and concludes "warnings-as-errors would fail here" happens to be right for the wrong reason; one that does the more rigorous thing and checks `$?` on the cheap probe concludes the opposite and is wrong. `mix compile` applies the setting as a task-level failure over the whole compilation; `elixirc`'s flag does not promote a file-level warning to a non-zero exit the same way.

**Correct alternative:** verify a mix-gate property with the mix gate. Create a throwaway project with `mix new`, put the minimal reproducing shape in its `lib/`, run the **exact** command the gate runs, and quote its exit code -- never a nearer-to-hand single-file compiler invocation that shares the flag name. The general rule this instantiates: **when the claim is about what a gate does, the probe must be the gate's own command.** A smaller tool that accepts the same flag is not a smaller version of the gate; it is a different program, and the difference will be in the exit code rather than in anything printed.
